top_story: After Washington threatened Iran’s power grid in March unless Tehran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran framed any pressure campaign as grounds for wider regional escalation, and that standoff hardened into repeated disruption of Gulf shipping in mid-April. Iran’s renewed closure of the strait on 19 April, including IRGC fire on a tanker during a brief reopening, was followed on 20 April by a US seizure of an Iran-flagged container ship, deepening the risk of miscalculation around a chokepoint that directly affects fuel prices, trade flows, and civilian livelihoods across the Gulf. In a related sign of regional containment efforts, Pakistan froze a $1.5 billion weapons sale to Sudan after Saudi objections, underscoring how Gulf powers are trying to limit secondary crises even as the Hormuz confrontation pulls security attention and economic confidence toward a more dangerous edge.
